paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the night before the cross, nothing caught Jesus off guard. He knew where the room would be, down to the man with the jug of water (Luke 22:10). He knew His betrayer was sitting close enough to share the table, and He said, "the Son of Man will go as it has been determined" (Luke 22:22). The plan was never slipping out of His hands.

Now look at what He does with that knowledge. He doesn't run, and He doesn't hide. He says, "I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before My suffering" (Luke 22:15). Then He hands over the bread, "This is My body, given for you," and the cup, "the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you" (Luke 22:19-20). He chose the cross for the very people at that table, and that includes the baker reading this right now.

And friend, don't skip the ending. When Jesus says a betrayer is at the table, the apostles don't point at one another. They "began to question among themselves which of them was going to do this" (Luke 22:23). I think that's a good question to carry into your own kitchen: not "who else?" but "Lord, keep me close." The bread and the cup tell us to "do this in remembrance of Me" (Luke 22:19), so remember Him today, because this story is NOT over.
